name: Dynamo Kyiv 1985-86 (Lobanovskyi)
scopeNote: Dynamo Kyiv under Valeriy Lobanovskyi, 1985 Soviet league and cup double and 1985/86 Cup Winners' Cup (final v Atletico Madrid, 3-0, Lyon, 2 May 1986), plus the 1986 Soviet league title won on 7 December 1986 (end date). Start date 1985-03-01 is approximate (first league match of the 1985 season, from memory, not verified). Sources call the style hard pressing, collective defending and fast counter-attacks, built on Lobanovskyi's scientific, 'universal' method; a 4-3-1-2 / 4-4-2 hybrid with Baltacha as sweeper. The USSR national team (1986 World Cup, Euro 88) and the 1975 Dynamo side are NOT part of this profile; the Spielverlagerung USSR analysis was not used as evidence. Marking (zonal vs man) in 1985-86 is not documented in the sources found.
openQuestions: Exact first match of the 1985 Soviet league season and exact date of the first CWC tie are unverified (memory only).
No 1985-86 source found stating zonal vs man-marking; later Dynamo/USSR sources describe mixed zonal and man-oriented defending.
The Hard Tackle says Lobanovskyi set 14 tasks for defenders and 13 for defenders (typo for attackers); cited via Wilson, check against Inverting the Pyramid.
Several sources (TFT) describe the 1986 shape as 4-3-1-2; the 4-4-2 label appears for USSR teams only.
No dated 1985-86 primary quote by Lobanovskyi found (stated-view and set-pieces left as gaps); the 'dialectic' and 'results stay' quotes are undated.

sources.title: These Football Times: Lobanovskyi and Dynamo Kyiv's scientific enlightenment
sources.evidence: The new Dynamo, lining up in a rough 4-3-1-2 system, were even more dynamic than before. With Baltacha as the complete sweeper, centre-half Oleh Kuznetsov was encouraged to push forward, something that suited him with his comfort on the ball.

sources.title: These Football Times: Lobanovskyi and Dynamo Kyiv's scientific enlightenment
sources.evidence: Zavarov was the most fluent player in the side, dropping so deep as to sometimes be dictating play from behind Kuznetsov.

sources.title: These Football Times: Lobanovskyi and Dynamo Kyiv's scientific enlightenment
sources.evidence: In turn, the full-backs, Beszonov and Demyanenko, were slightly more conservative than their forebears.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: high pressing, precision of passing and economy of movement. Without ball there would be two to three players pressing their opponents

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: Chanov started the move by throwing towards Demyanenko who took two touches before launching a long pass for Belanov. Belanov held off both Spanish center-backs before rolling a pass for Blokhin who shot wide.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: When going on the offensive the tireless Demyanenko overlapped, increasing the man advantage in midfield which allowed Dynamo to press better.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: Blokhin, one of the greatest goalscorers of his generation frequently drifted out as an attacking left or right winger, making late runs in the box unmarked.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: Dynamo seemed to relax a bit after the half hour mark though their opponents failed to threaten Chanov in that period.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: He would lay down a set of 14 tasks for his defenders and 13 for his defenders, prepared after minute study of opponent team.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: Scoring an average of two goals per match the Bilo Syni nicked the league with just two points separating them from Spartak Moscow. Local rival Shakhtar Donetsk was edged out 1-0 in a tight Soviet Cup final as Dynamo sealed the double.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: Dynamo began the Cup Winners Cup campaign with a stutter, losing the away leg in Utrecht 2-1 and trailing 1-0 with just eight minutes gone in Kyiv. However, they came back strongly, scoring four times before the hour mark to win 5-3 on aggregate.

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: Growing in confidence Dynamo made mincemeat of Rapid Vienna, finalists the previous year, winning both legs by 1-4 and 5-1 scorelines. A 3-0 win against fellow Eastern Europeans Dukla Prague in the first leg more or less sealed their passage

sources.title: The Hard Tackle: Dynamo Kyiv 3-0 Atletico Madrid
sources.evidence: Dynamo Kyiv was just coming off a highly successful season after winning their first league-Cup double in more than one decade.

sources.evidence: Loba supplemented these signings by nurturing homegrown talent such as right-back Volodymyr Beszonov, sweeper Sergei Baltacha. and attacking midfielder Oleksiy Mykhaylychenko. These players would form the nucleus of another great Dynamo team.

sources.title: These Football Times: Lobanovskyi and Dynamo Kyiv's scientific enlightenment
sources.evidence: Now well into his 30s, he was unable to lead the line and run the channels with the same exuberance as he had done in his youth. Fortunately, Lobanovskyi had provided him with added support in the form of the mercurial Igor Belanov. Behind them Oleksandr Zavarov schemed, seeking openings for through balls or shots.

sources.title: These Football Times: Lobanovskyi and Dynamo Kyiv's scientific enlightenment
sources.evidence: Dynamo responded to the pressure by countering at high speed. With five minutes left, Rats ran down the left and passed inside to Belanov

sources.title: Dynamo Kyiv site: Lipenko column, Chronicle of the Total Triumph of 1986
sources.evidence: Due to the participation of 12 players from the Kyiv club in the 1986 World Cup in Mexico, its matches in the domestic arena were constantly postponed. Therefore, from July 4 to December 7, the Kyiv Dynamo played 23 (!) matches in the championship.

sources.title: Dynamo Kyiv site: Lipenko column, Chronicle of the Total Triumph of 1986
sources.evidence: Chanov and Ratz played all 30 matches, Demyanenko 29, Yakovenko 28, Yevtushenko and Kuznetsov 27 each, Bal 26, Blokhin 23, Belanov 22, Mikhaylichenko and Zavarov 20 each, Bessonov 16, Yevseyev and Yaremchuk 15 each, Baltacha 13

sources.title: Dynamo Kyiv site: Lipenko column, Chronicle of the Total Triumph of 1986
sources.evidence: In that championship, Kyiv scored 53 goals against 15 opponents and conceded 33.

sources.title: Dynamo Kyiv site: Lipenko column, Cup trophy and gold of the championship
sources.evidence: In 30 matches of the championship the Kyivians scored 53 goals in the opponents' gates, having conceded 33. The most productive player for Dynamo was Belanov, who scored 10 goals.

sources.title: Dynamo Kyiv site: Lipenko column, Cup trophy and gold of the championship
sources.evidence: In the final match of the championship on the 7th of December on their field with the score 2:1 the Kyivians defeated their Moscow teammates, their main pursuers.

sources.title: These Football Times: Lobanovskyi and Dynamo Kyiv's scientific enlightenment
sources.evidence: He was capable of throwing in the occasional Marxist buzzword, like when he stated, “If an opponent has found a counter-play, then we need to find a new strategy. That is the dialectic of the game.”
